Reviewers reportedly recommended contacting police, but the account was instead deactivated, after which the shooter continued using ChatGPT through another account, according to the filing.

The February 10 attack killed eight people, including five children and an educational assistant, while 27 others were wounded. The attacker also killed her mother and sibling before dying by suicide.
British Columbia is seeking damages for costs tied to the community’s recovery and rebuilding, along with court-ordered changes to OpenAI’s
handling of conversations involving potential violence. The province said it is also pursuing stronger AI safeguards and accountability measures.
